messages:
Sam (Support): Heads up — customer ticket #4852. They say streaming endpoints have very low TTFB (~30-60ms) but p95/p99 total time jumped ~3x since yesterday. Non-streaming (single response) looks normal. They attached traces and say chunking looks irregular. Repro steps below.

Alex (Eng Runtime): Can you paste the raw request they used? Also which model and deployment (Dedicated pool id)?

Sam (Support): They are on Dedicated pool d-42eu, model: open-rw-7b, SDK & curl both used. Repro (simplified):
```\ncurl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true" \n  -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":800}'\n```
They reported TTFB ~40ms but last byte at 2.4s for p95 yesterday -> now p95 ~7.3s.

Maria (SRE): @Alex @Olivia any infra changes around the rollout window? I see a runtime push 2026-03-14 22:12 to the dedicated fleet labelled "stream-autoflush" (horizon-bot deploy event below). Could be related to flush policy.

horizon-bot: Deploy d-42eu @2026-03-14T22:12:44Z — change: runtime: adjust auto-flush heuristics (PR #1179) :gear:

Alex (Eng Runtime): Thanks. That PR tuned the flush threshold to reduce tiny-chunk spam by aggregating 30-50ms of tokens before flushing. That saved money but could increase tail if client expects steady micro-chunks. Might explain TTFB vs total delta if prefixes aren't flushed.

Olivia (Oncall): Sam can you confirm whether the customer is using HTTP/1 chunked streaming or SSE over HTTP/2? Different buffers in proxies.

Sam (Support): They said they used both. Primary issue observed with SSE/HTTP2 via their app. I asked for curl with `-v` and `--http2` and they sent back a snippet showing `transfer-encoding: chunked` on our side and `:status 200`.

Raj (Eng ML): Two angles: 1) server flush policy changed -> larger initial prefix aggregation increases end-to-end for long requests (client waits for second flush). 2) KV/prefix cache miss pattern -> first tokens expensive while subsequent tokens faster. But customer sees low TTFB so initial API ack is fast. That points to batching/flush timing rather than compute startup.

Alex (Eng Runtime): Agreed. Let's collect metrics: per-request flush count, flush intervals histogram, bytes per flush, and client-visible chunk timestamps. Can SRE pull logs from d-42eu for the time window?

Maria (SRE): Pulling. Also checking nginx/proxy configs — if nginx proxy_buffering is on it can coalesce chunks. For HTTP/2, some proxies reframe SSE. I'll get proxy logs and tcpdump on the LB to compare chunk spacing at the edge vs on the server.

Sam (Support): Customer also attached a trace where they measured chunk arrival times at the browser: initial chunk at 50ms, then long pause ~6s, then big chunk. They said it used to be more even micro-chunks. :frowning:

Olivia (Oncall): Quick repro steps we asked them to run locally (use these please):
```\n# measure time to first byte + total with streaming
curl -s -w "TTFB:%{time_starttransfer}s TOTAL:%{time_total}s\n" -o /dev/null -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  --http2 \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true" -d '{"prompt":"lorem","max_tokens":120}'\n# non-streaming compare
curl -s -w "TOTAL:%{time_total}s\n" -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=false" -d '{"prompt":"lorem","max_tokens":120}'\n```
Please run both and paste outputs + `-v` headers when possible.

Sam (Support): Customer ran those, pasted results: streaming TTFB 0.05s TOTAL 7.2s, non-streaming TOTAL 0.9s. They included a screenshot of chunk arrival timings in-browser.

Alex (Eng Runtime): That looks like server is buffering multiple tokens and sending once threshold met. Options: rollback the auto-flush PR, or tweak policy to preserve shorter-first-flush behavior for Dedicated customers. Short-term mitigation: set a per-deployment flag `stream.force_early_flush=true` that reduces aggregation to 5-10ms. Can we flip that for d-42eu?

Maria (SRE): We can toggle runtime flags for the pool. I need sign-off and customer consent to test. Also will check if any intermediate LBs are coalescing.

Raj (Eng ML): Also check model tokenizer behavior — if the model returns large early tokens (e.g., long whitespace) then chunking semantics differ. But given non-streaming is faster it's purely flush.

Sam (Support): Customer is OK with A/B test. They prefer not to roll back the whole deploy. They asked for a setting to make streaming behave like before.

Olivia (Oncall): Plan: 1) SRE toggles `stream.force_early_flush=true` for pool d-42eu (canary to 10% of capacity) 2) Monitor p50/p95/p99 for streaming total time and per-flush spacing 3) If improvement, roll to 100% 4) Engineering to follow up to make flush policy configurable per-customer. Trigger: deploy flag set now.

Alex (Eng Runtime): I'll prepare a quick revert patch in case flag doesn't help. Also logging: add `x-flush-count` and `x-last-flush-ms` response headers for debugging -> we can ship in 1-2 hours if needed.

horizon-bot: Flag update executed for d-42eu: stream.force_early_flush=canary(10%) by Maria @2026-03-14T23:03:12Z

Maria (SRE): Canary metrics after 3 minutes: streaming p95 total dropped from 7.3s -> 1.1s for canary instances, p50 unchanged. Proxy chunk timings show more frequent small chunks leaving server. Edge LB buffer still off.

Sam (Support): Customer confirmed improved behavior on canary endpoint — total times back to expected. They are happy with canary results. :thumbsup:

Raj (Eng ML): Next actions for Eng: make flush policy per-deployment configurable and add observability headers. Also run a short perf cost analysis (more frequent flushes -> slightly higher token cost). I'll own the perf delta numbers.

Alex (Eng Runtime): I'll open a follow-up PR to revert the global aggressive aggregation and add a per-deployment tunable. Link to follow-up PR in this thread once ready.

Sam (Support): I'll update ticket #4852 and ask customer if they'd like the new flag permanently set. Thanks team.

Olivia (Oncall): Notes for postmortem: cause = runtime auto-flush aggregation change + proxy-friendly defaults; immediate mitigation = canary early-flush flag; long-term = config per-pool + headers + test coverage for streaming latency.

Sam (Support): Closing loop with customer now. If anyone wants the raw traces/screenshots I can add to the ticket.

Alex (Eng Runtime): Please attach them. Also include the canary metric graphs. Good catch everyone. :eyes:
